statement: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 6, including n=0 under the convention fixed in problem.md, every finite simple graph G on the labelled vertex set {1,...,n} is Hall-universal: for every simple graph H on that same labelled set, the Hilton--Johnson Hall inequalities for the graphic lists L_G(v)=N_G(v) imply the existence of a proper L_G-coloring of H. Up to isomorphism the complete positive census has 1, 1, 2, 4, 11, 34, and 156 classes in orders n=0,...,6, and there are no negative classes.
contribution: This is a full exact computational resolution of the frozen finite census, not a claimed solution of the source paper's unrestricted characterization problem. It records independently verified per-H Hall and colorability bits for all 209 canonical G, with full labelled-G orbit verification and row/aggregate SHA-256 bindings. Of the 209 positive classes, 199 are certified by explicitly recognized families in the cited source; the first of the ten remaining classes in (n,graph6) order is the five-vertex bull graph DBk. The limited literature screen does not establish priority.
